en: The largest pattern there is: galaxies are not scattered at random but strung along filaments and sheets around near-empty voids, a structure that looks like foam or a web of glowing threads. This shell is a heavily schematic model — a diagram of the idea, not a survey — showing a handful of the great walls, superclusters, and voids of the nearby universe. It is the fossil of tiny ripples in the infant cosmos, grown over billions of years by gravity.
cur: 最大的图案：星系并非随机分布，而是沿着丝状结构和薄片排列，围绕近乎空洞的区域，形成类似泡沫或发光丝线网络的结构。这个壳层是高度示意的模型——概念图示而非观测数据——展示了附近宇宙中的若干伟大墙面、超星系团和空洞。它是婴儿宇宙中微小涟漪的化石，在数十亿年间被引力放大。

en: 'Immense heaven' in Hawaiian — the supercluster defined in 2014 not by where galaxies sit but by where they flow. Some 160 megaparsecs (500 million light-years) across, containing about 100,000 galaxies, Laniakea is the basin of attraction our Virgo Supercluster drains into, toward the Great Attractor. And Laniakea, with its neighbours, is part of a broader flow toward something larger still: the Shapley Concentration.
cur: '夏威夷语中意为'广阔的天空' — 2014年定义的超星系团，不是按星系所处位置而是按星系流动方向来划分。Laniakea超星系团跨度约160百万秒差距（5亿光年），包含约10万个星系，是我们本星系群引力流向之处，朝向巨引源方向。Laniakea及其邻近星系团都是一个更大引力流的组成部分：夏普力超星系团。

en: The Milky Way, Andromeda, the Triangulum galaxy and dozens of smaller companions, bound by gravity across some 10 million light-years. Andromeda and the Milky Way are drifting toward each other and may merge a few billion years from now — recent simulations put it closer to a coin-flip.
cur: 银河系、Andromeda、Triangulum以及数十个较小的伴星系，在约1000万光年的范围内由重力束缚。Andromeda和银河系正在相互漂移，可能在数十亿年后合并 — 最近的模拟将其描述得更像一枚硬币的概率。

en: The galaxy groups just beyond the Local Group lie in a thin, nearly flat layer — the Local Sheet — moving together within the wider Local Volume. It is a first glimpse of the cosmic web's geometry: galaxies are not scattered at random but tend to lie along sheets and filaments.
cur: 本星系群外的星系群位于一个薄的、近似平坦的层面 — 本星系板 — 在更广的本星系团内一起运动。这是对宇宙网几何结构的初一瞥：星系并非随机散布，而是倾向于沿着薄板和丝状体分布。

en: A barred spiral of a few hundred billion stars, about 100,000 light-years across. The overlays show what the eye can't: the nearly flat rotation curve, the dark-matter halo it implies, and the stellar populations that record how the disc, bulge and halo were built.
cur: 一个数千亿颗恒星的棒旋星系，约10万光年宽。叠加图层显示肉眼看不到的内容：近似平坦的旋转曲线、它所暗示的暗物质晕，以及记录盘、凸起和晕如何构成的恒星族群。

en: The Sun's nearest stars, placed at their true distances and colours. The teaching layers trace the constellation figures, pick out the deep-sky objects, sort the stars on the Hertzsprung–Russell diagram, and ripple light-travel time outward from the Sun.
cur: 太阳最近的恒星，按其真实距离和颜色放置。教学图层勾勒星座图形，挑选深空天体，在Hertzsprung–Russell图上对恒星进行分类，并从太阳向外波及光行时。

en: Our home supercluster — a hundred or more galaxy groups and clusters spread across some 33 megaparsecs (about 110 million light-years, and larger by some definitions), dominated by the Virgo Cluster. It was long thought the largest structure we belong to; Laniakea later revealed it to be one lobe of something far bigger.
cur: 我们的家乡超星系团 — 超过一百个星系群和星系团散布在约33兆秒差距（约1.1亿光年，按某些定义更大）的范围内，由室女座星系团主导。人们长期以为它是我们所属的最大结构；后来Laniakea的发现揭示它只是更庞大天体的一个叶瓣。

en: Closer to the horizon, time runs slower relative to a far-away clock — the factor is √(1 − rₛ/r). Shown for a non-spinning black hole; real spinning ones shift the photon sphere and orbits inward.
cur: 越靠近视界,时间相对于远方时钟流逝越慢——系数为 √(1 − rₛ/r)。此处展示无自旋黑洞;真实自旋黑洞会将光子球层和轨道向内移动。

en: A small, faint dwarf galaxy — one of the dozens that populate the Local Group.
cur: 一个小而暗淡的矮星系——本星系群中数十个矮星系之一。

en: A gas-rich irregular galaxy with no ordered shape, lit by bursts of new star formation.
cur: 富含气体的不规则星系,形态无序,由新恒星形成的爆发照亮。

en: One of the Local Group's grand spiral galaxies — hundreds of billions of stars in a rotating disk of arms, gas, and dust.
cur: 本星系群的宏伟旋涡星系之一——数千亿颗恒星组成旋转的旋臂盘面,充满气体和尘埃。

en: You are here. The whole Local Group — the Milky Way, Andromeda, and their dozens of companions — is a single dot at this scale, one member of the wider Local Sheet.
cur: 你在这里。整个本星系群——银河系、Andromeda及其数十个伴星系——在这个尺度上只是一个点，是更广阔的本地片层中的一个成员。

en: A gravitationally bound, if loosely structured, collection of galaxies just beyond the Local Group. It belongs to the Local Sheet — a thin, roughly planar slab of nearby galaxy groups about 10 megaparsecs across — itself embedded in the wider Local Volume, the ~10-Mpc-radius sphere astronomers have mapped galaxy by galaxy.
cur: 一个引力束缚的、虽然结构松散的星系集合，位于本星系群之外。它属于本地片层——一个厚度较薄、大致平面的邻近星系群薄板，跨度约10百万秒差距——本身嵌入在更广阔的本地体积中，这是天文学家已绘制的星系分布范围，半径约为10百万秒差距的球体。

en: Every known planet in our catalogue, re-plotted by mass and orbit. The lit path is this system — see where it sits among the rest, and next to our own worlds.
cur: 我们星表中的所有已知行星,按质量和轨道重新绘制。高亮路径是此系统——看它在众多系统中的位置,以及与我们太阳系的对比。

en: A spiral arm. In the leading density-wave model it isn't a fixed set of stars but a travelling wave, where gas piles up, compresses, and lights up in bright new star formation — though whether the arms are long-lived waves or shorter-lived features is still debated.
cur: 旋臂。在领先密度波模型中，它不是一组固定的恒星，而是一列行进的密度波，其中气体堆积、压缩，并因明亮的新星形成而发光——但旋臂究竟是长期存在的波还是短期特征仍在争论中。

en: An ancient globular cluster — hundreds of thousands of stars bound by gravity into a dense sphere, orbiting far out in the Galactic halo. Among the oldest objects in the Milky Way, nearly as old as the Universe itself.
cur: 一个古老的球状星团——数十万颗恒星被引力束缚成一个致密球体，在银河晕的远处绕行。是银河系中最古老的天体之一，年龄几乎与宇宙本身相当。

cur: 暗物质晕 · 推断得出，质量约为可见物质的15–20倍

en: Closing on the destination. V∞ is the excess speed at infinity — the speed the spacecraft would have if the planet's gravity weren't there. It sets the minimum braking ∆v before any orbit insertion.
cur: 接近目的地。V∞是无穷远处的超速——如果没有行星引力,航天器将具有的速度。它决定了任何入轨前所需的最小制动∆v。

en: The arrival burn slows the vehicle from its hyperbolic V∞ down below the destination's escape velocity, capturing it into a closed orbit. Miss this burn and the spacecraft flies past forever.
cur: 抵达点火将飞行器从双曲线V∞减速至低于目的地逃逸速度,使其被捕获进入闭合轨道。错过此次点火,航天器将永远飞离。

en: Coasting along a Hohmann transfer — the most fuel-efficient ellipse that touches both planets' orbits. The Sun is the only force; vis-viva gives the speed at every point. No fuel burning, no engine — coast time is free.
cur: 沿着Hohmann转移轨道滑行——一条触及两颗行星轨道的最省燃料椭圆。太阳是唯一的作用力；活力方程(vis-viva)给出每一点的速度。不燃烧燃料，不启动引擎——滑行时间是免费的。

en: C3 is the squared launch energy a vehicle has after escaping Earth. A positive C3 means the spacecraft is leaving Earth's gravity well; the higher the number, the faster the cruise.
cur: C3是飞行器逃离地球后具有的发射能量平方。正C3意味着航天器正在离开地球引力井；数值越高,巡航速度越快。

en: The injection burn (TLI for the Moon, TMI for Mars) is the largest single ∆v of the trip. After it, the engine is off and the vehicle coasts on a Keplerian arc all the way to the destination.

cur: 所需 Δv 为地球近地轨道（含损耗）

en: Δv from the departure planet's solar orbit (excludes launch + escape)
cur: 从出发行星的日心轨道计算的Δv（不含发射与逃逸）

en: Gravity loss approximated as constant-g × burn time
cur: 重力损失近似为恒定重力加速度 × 点火时间

en: This formula could not be evaluated with these inputs.
cur: 无法使用这些输入计算此公式。

en: Invalid wire — step {step} has no output named {output}.
cur: 连线无效——步骤 {step} 没有名为 {output} 的输出。

en: Upstream failed — step {step} produced no value to wire in.
cur: 上游失败——步骤 {step} 未产生可供连线的数值。

en: Impact too hard for airbags — slow down more first (a retro burn, as Pathfinder did).
cur: 撞击速度过高，气囊无法承受——请先进一步减速（像Pathfinder那样做一次反推点火）。

en: Orbital speed and burn time must be real, non-negative numbers.
cur: 轨道速度和点火时间必须为非负实数。

en: Thrust-to-weight must exceed 1 — below it you cannot slow the fall, you crash.
cur: 推重比必须大于 1——低于 1 则无法减缓下降，将会坠毁。

en: Not enough delta-v to reach the target — the vehicle falls short.
cur: delta-v 不足以到达目标——飞行器无法抵达。

en: That world isn't on a tabulated heliocentric orbit here.
cur: 该天体不在此处列出的日心轨道数据中。

en: Departure and arrival must be different worlds.
cur: 出发天体与抵达天体必须不同。

en: That world isn't one you can orbit here — choose Earth or the Moon.
cur: 该天体无法在此绕行——请选择地球或月球。

en: Too fast to touch down — you need a powered descent (the sky-crane).
cur: 速度过快，无法着陆——你需要动力下降（空中吊车）。

en: No atmosphere here — drag can't slow you at all; a burn is the only way down.
cur: 这里没有大气——阻力无法减速；只能靠点火下降。

en: The loaded mass must be greater than the empty mass — a rocket has to carry propellant to burn.
cur: 满载质量必须大于空载质量——火箭必须携带可燃烧的推进剂。

en: Thrust is below weight — the vehicle stays on the pad.
cur: 推力小于重力——飞行器仍留在发射台上。

en: That distance isn't on this orbit — a point must satisfy r < 2a.
cur: 该距离不在此轨道上——点必须满足 r < 2a。

en: You don't aim at Mars; you aim at where Mars will be. Find the transfer orbit and the launch window that put you both in the same place, months later.
cur: 你瞄准的不是火星，而是火星将会到达的位置。找到那条转移轨道和发射窗口，让你们数月后在同一处相遇。

en: Mars rides a bigger, slower orbit around the Sun. The same Hohmann trick as the Moon, one scale up: one burn to swing out to Mars’s orbit, coast a long arc across the solar system, one burn to arrive.
cur: 火星沿着一条更大、更慢的日心轨道运行。与飞往月球相同的Hohmann技巧，只是尺度更大：一次点火摆到火星轨道，沿一条横跨太阳系的长弧滑行，再一次点火抵达。

en: Do you have the Δv to make the crossing? This is the Δv from Earth's orbit around the Sun — on top of everything it took to leave Earth in the first place.
cur: 你有足够的Δv完成这次跨越吗？这是从地球绕太阳的轨道算起的Δv——还要在此之前一切离开地球所需的量之上。

en: You can't leave whenever you like — Earth and Mars must be lined up so Mars is actually there when your arc reaches its orbit. That alignment only comes around about every 26 months.
cur: 你不能随时出发——地球与火星必须对齐，好让你的飞行弧抵达火星轨道时火星恰好在那里。这样的对齐大约每26个月才出现一次。

en: Just enough air to burn you, not enough to stop you. Chain heat shield, parachute and rockets into the 'seven minutes of terror'.
cur: 空气刚好够烧灼你，却不足以让你停下。将隔热罩、降落伞与火箭串联起来，度过“恐怖七分钟”。

en: No air means no parachute — the only brake is the engine. Fly the descent burn that sets you down gently on an airless world.
cur: 没有空气就没有降落伞——唯一的刹车就是发动机。飞完这段下降点火，在无空气的世界上轻柔着陆。

en: The thickest air in the inner system — a furnace under crushing pressure. See how that dense atmosphere both slows your fall and fights you all the way down.
cur: 内太阳系最浓厚的大气——高压之下的一座熔炉。看这稠密的大气如何既减缓你的坠落，又一路与你抗争到底。

en: It all starts with one law: a force changes a mass's motion. Push harder, or make it lighter, and it speeds up faster.
cur: 一切始于一条定律：力改变质量的运动。推得更用力，或让它更轻，它就加速得更快。

en: Where on Earth you launch from is a free head start: the planet's spin already carries the pad eastward — fastest at the equator, nothing at the poles. That is why Ariane flies from Kourou, and why companies tow platforms out to sea.
cur: 你在地球上从哪里发射就是一份免费的初始优势：行星的自转已经把发射台向东带动——赤道最快，两极为零。这正是Ariane从库鲁发射的原因，也是企业把平台拖到海上的原因。

en: A rocket moves by throwing mass out the back. The momentum it gives the exhaust is the momentum it gains going forward.
cur: 火箭靠向后抛出质量前进。它赋予喷流的动量，就是它前进所获得的动量。

en: How much Δv does orbit actually demand? Not a magic number — it is the orbital speed you must reach (set by this world’s gravity and size) plus the losses fighting up through gravity and air. On Earth about 9.4 km/s; a smaller, airless world asks far less.
cur: 入轨实际需要多少Δv？这并非魔法数字——它是你必须达到的轨道速度（由该天体的引力和大小决定），再加上对抗引力和空气爬升所付出的损耗。地球约为9.4 km/s；更小、无大气的天体所需则要少得多。

en: Burning propellant builds up speed. The rocket equation ties how fast the exhaust leaves and how much propellant you carry to the delta-v you gain.
cur: 燃烧推进剂积累速度。火箭方程将喷流的喷出速度和携带的推进剂量，与你获得的 delta-v 联系起来。

en: For liftoff, thrust has to beat weight. If the thrust-to-weight ratio is below one, the rocket never leaves the pad.
cur: 要起飞，推力必须胜过重力。若推重比低于一，火箭永远离不开发射台。

en: Now add it up: your rocket's Δv plus the free head-start from your launch site, against what orbit demands. A better site buys margin — or lets you fly a smaller rocket for the same job.
cur: 现在算一算：火箭的 Δv 加上发射场带来的免费初速，对比轨道所需的能量。更好的发射场带来余量——或让你用更小的火箭完成同样的任务。

en: Gravity pulls on every mass with a force we call weight. To leave the ground, something has to push back harder than this.
cur: 引力以一种我们称为重力的力拉扯每一份质量。要离开地面，必须有物体推得比它更用力。

en: Start where every flight starts: a force, a mass, and Newton's laws. Push harder or fly lighter, and watch exactly how much faster you go.
cur: 从每次飞行的起点开始：一个力、一份质量，以及Newton定律。推得更猛或飞得更轻，看你究竟能加速多少。

en: The cheap way the early rovers landed: bounce down inside inflated airbags. But they only survive so hard a hit — about 25 m/s. Your parachute leaves you faster than that, so airbags alone will not do it either; Pathfinder fired small retros first to slow down before it bounced.
cur: 早期火星车着陆的廉价方式：裹在充气气囊里弹跳落地。但气囊只能承受一定强度的撞击——约 25 m/s。你的降落伞留给你的速度高于此值，所以单靠气囊也不行；Pathfinder在弹跳前先点燃小型反推火箭来减速。

en: So you deploy the biggest parachute the airflow will allow. It helps — but on Mars even a huge chute only gets you down to tens of metres per second. Still not survivable.
cur: 于是你展开气流所能承受的最大降落伞。它有帮助——但在火星上，即使是巨型降落伞也只能把速度降到每秒数十米。仍然无法幸存。

en: So you add a retro-booster: it fires downward to kill the speed the parachute could not. The two methods together — free drag plus paid thrust — are how you actually land. On the airless Moon the parachute does nothing and the booster does it all; on Earth the chute alone is enough. Same physics, different world.
cur: 于是你加装了反推助推器：它向下点火，抵消降落伞无法消除的速度。两种方式结合——免费的气动阻力加上耗费燃料的推力——才是真正实现着陆的方法。在没有大气的月球上，降落伞毫无作用，全靠助推器；而在地球上，仅靠降落伞就足够了。相同的物理原理，不同的世界。

en: Mars has air — but barely. A capsule falling through it reaches terminal velocity, where drag balances weight. Because the air is roughly one-sixtieth of Earth's, that speed is still hundreds of metres per second.
cur: 火星有大气——但极其稀薄。返回舱穿过大气时会达到末速度，此时阻力与重力平衡。由于其大气密度约为地球的六十分之一，该速度仍高达每秒数百米。

en: Compare your terminal speed to a safe touchdown. On Mars you come up short — the thin air can't finish the job, so you must fire engines the rest of the way. That is why every Mars lander ends under power.
cur: 将你的末速度与安全着陆速度对比。在火星上你无法达标——稀薄的大气无法完成任务，因此你必须在剩余路程点火发动机。这就是为什么每个火星着陆器最终都要靠动力着陆。

en: Thick cold air and gentle gravity make Titan the easiest big world to land on — a parachute alone can do it. Fly Huygens' drift through the orange haze.
cur: 浓密寒冷的大气与轻柔的引力，使土卫六成为最易着陆的大型天体——仅凭降落伞就能完成。驾驭Huygens号穿越橙色雾霭的漂降。

en: There is no surface — only deeper, hotter, denser gas. Plunge a probe into the giant and watch the atmosphere tear at it as it falls.
cur: 这里没有表面——只有越来越深、越来越热、越来越稠密的气体。将探测器投入这颗巨行星，看大气在它坠落时将它撕扯。

en: Jupiter's gravity hurls you in at 47 km/s — over four times faster than any return to Earth. At that speed the survivable band of entry angles narrows brutally: a shade too steep and even a probe built like a cannonball is crushed; too shallow and you graze off having crossed half the solar system for nothing. This card's ballistic bound already squeezes the band to a several-degree slot — and the real corridor was tighter still: heating and single-pass capture, physics beyond this simple model, forced Galileo's navigators to thread ±1.5° of sky around −8.6°.
cur: 木星的引力以47 km/s的速度将你拉进去——比任何地球返回速度快四倍多。以这种速度，可生存的进入角度范围急剧缩小：稍陡一点，即使是像炮弹一样坚硬的探测器也会被压碎；太浅则会在跨越半个太阳系后掠过而功亏一篑。这张卡牌的弹道约束已将范围挤压到几度的狭槽——而真实走廊还要更窄：加热和单次捕获等超出这个简单模型的物理现象，迫使Galileo号的导航员在−8.6°周围线程±1.5°的天空。

en: Then comes the entry itself — the fastest atmospheric entry any craft has survived. The probe met the hydrogen at 47.4 km/s and decelerated at about 228 g, its shield shedding more than half its mass as glowing gas in under two minutes. Every crewed-entry rule of thumb dies here; this is survivable by machines alone.
cur: 接着是进入过程本身——有史以来最快的一次。探测器以47.4 km/s的速度撞入氢气，减速约230 g，其热护盾在两分钟内脱落了超过一半的质量，化为炽热的气体。在这里，所有有人进入的经验法则都失效了；只有机器才能生存。

en: And then — nothing to land on. Under its parachute the probe just kept sinking, and the sky surprised everyone: it had fallen into a strangely dry, cloud-sparse 'hot spot', with about ten times less water than the textbooks predicted. There is no touchdown rung in this lesson because no touchdown exists: after nearly 58 minutes and ~23 bar of pressure, Jupiter simply crushed and swallowed it. The probe's data outlived the probe.
cur: 然后——没有着陆点。在降落伞下，探测器不断下沉，穿过氨云和水云，周围的空气越来越稠密。这节课中没有着陆的阶段，因为着陆点根本不存在：在58分钟和约23巴的压力后，木星最终压碎并吞没了它。探测器的数据比探测器本身活得更久。

en: Galileo's atmospheric probe is the only entry probe ever to fly into a giant planet's atmosphere and report back. Its 57.6 minutes of transmission rewrote the textbooks on Jupiter's winds, water and helium — and its entry remains the extreme benchmark of atmospheric flight: no object has ever hit an atmosphere faster and survived to speak.
cur: Galileo的大气探测器是唯一进入巨行星大气并传回信息的航天器。它57.6分钟的传输时间重新改写了关于木星风速、水含量和氦含量的教科书——其进入过程仍然是大气飞行的极限基准：没有任何物体以更快的速度撞入大气并存活到能够传输数据。

en: The probe's signal died 57.6 minutes in — not from a fault, but because Jupiter's heat and pressure destroyed it. Its mothership listened until there was nothing left to hear.
cur: 探针的信号在57.6分钟后消失——并非源于故障,而是因为木星的热量和压力摧毁了它。它的母船一直在聆听,直到再也没有任何声音可以接收。

en: Galileo — the mission that carried the probe (NASA)
cur: Galileo——运载探测器的任务（NASA）

en: Juno — flying Jupiter's poles today (NASA)
cur: Juno——今天在木星两极飞行（NASA）

en: Next: the smallest worlds — landing where gravity barely exists.
cur: 下一个：最小的世界——着陆在引力几乎不存在的地方。

en: So fifteen minutes in, Huygens let the big chute go and swapped to a drogue smaller than a beach umbrella. Even under that scrap of fabric, Titan's air lands you at under 5 m/s — a firm bump into frozen mud. The gentlest landing in the solar system, bought with the smallest parachute.
cur: 所以在下降15分钟后，Huygens号释放了主降落伞，换上了一个比沙滩伞还小的小型降落伞。即使在这块布料下，泰坦的空气也会让你以不到5米/秒的速度着陆——对冰冻泥浆的有力撞击。太阳系中最温柔的着陆，用最小的降落伞买来的。

en: Titan hides under a nitrogen atmosphere half again as thick as Earth's at the surface, and it reaches high — Huygens started feeling it over a thousand kilometres up. Coming in at 6 km/s the probe pulled over a dozen g behind its shield: a real re-entry, at a moon.
cur: 土卫六藏身于一层氮气大气之下,其地表气压约为地球的一点五倍,而且大气层向上延伸得很高——Huygens 在一千多公里的高空就已开始感受到它的存在。探测器以 6 km/s 的速度进入,在防热罩后承受了十几个 g 的过载:这是一次真正的再入,而且发生在一颗卫星上。

en: Pop a full-sized parachute here and you fall at walking pace — which sounds perfect and is actually fatal. Titan's air is so thick and its gravity so weak that under Huygens' 8.3-metre main chute the probe would drift for many hours, and its batteries had less than three in them. On Titan the parachute paradox cuts the other way: too much drag kills you slowly.
cur: 在这里打开全尺寸降落伞，你会以步行速度下降——听起来很完美，实际上是致命的。泰坦的空气太稠密，重力太弱，在Huygens号的8.3米主降落伞下，探测器会漂浮数小时，但电池只能维持不到三小时。在泰坦上，降落伞悖论反了过来：过大的阻力会慢慢杀死你。

en: Check the touchdown: the drogue delivers you slower than the probe's design limit. Titan passes with a hand-sized parachute and no engine — the only world besides Earth where a soft landing is this cheap. The price was paid elsewhere: seven years of cruising just to arrive.
cur: 检查着陆情况：小型降落伞让你的速度低于探测器设计极限。泰坦通过了考验，仅用一个手掌大小的降落伞和无发动机就实现了软着陆——除地球外唯一能这么便宜实现软着陆的世界。代价在别处付出：七年的航行才能到达。

en: So Venera let go of its parachute at about 47–50 km — deliberately — and fell the last hour on nothing but its flat aeroshell disc. In air this thick, even that lands you at roughly 7 m/s, about the speed of dropping off a garden wall. Drag alone does what Mars needed rockets for.
cur: 因此Venera号在约47–50公里高度故意抛弃了降落伞，仅凭其平坦的气动罩盘坠落最后一个小时。在如此稠密的大气中，即使这样的着陆速度也仅约7米/秒，相当于从花园围墙跳下的速度。仅凭阻力就完成了火星需要火箭才能做到的事。

en: Open a parachute in Venus's lower atmosphere and you drift down at walking pace — but that gentleness is a trap: the descent would take so long that the heat would kill the lander before the ground does. Watch what the same chute that barely helped on Mars does here.
cur: 在金星下层大气中打开降落伞，你会以行走速度缓慢下降——但这种温和正是陷阱：下降耗时太长，热量会在地面之前杀死着陆器。看看在火星上几乎没有帮助的同一降落伞在这里会如何表现。

en: On Mars the entry corridor is a knife-edge; here it is a barn door. Air this dense will capture you across a huge band of entry angles — the Venera probes dove in steeply on purpose to shorten the trip through the furnace. Getting captured is not the problem on Venus.
cur: 在火星上进入走廊是刀锋一线；这里则是大门洞开。如此稠密的大气会在广泛的进入角度范围内捕获你——Venera探测器故意陡峭俯冲以缩短通过炉火的时间。被捕获在金星上不是问题。

en: Venus meets you with an atmosphere about ninety times Earth's surface pressure. Hit it directly from interplanetary speed at a steep angle and it stops you almost at once — the deceleration peaks above a hundred g. No crew could ride this; the Venera landers were built like submarines and took it.
cur: 金星迎接你的是大约为地表压力九十倍的大气。以陡峭角度从行星际速度直接撞入它，它几乎立即停止你——减速峰值超过一百g。任何船员都无法承受；Venera着陆器像潜艇一样建造，能够承受这一切。

en: Check the touchdown: the aeroshell-only fall arrives slower than the shock ring can survive. Venus passes with no retro-rockets and no parachute at the surface — the exact inverse of Mars. The real enemy waits after landing: at ~460 °C, the lander has about an hour to live.
cur: 检查着陆：仅有气动外壳的下降到达速度比冲击环能承受的更慢。金星不使用制动火箭和表面降落伞就通过了——这正好与火星相反。真正的敌人在着陆后等待：在约460°C下，着陆器只能存活大约一小时。

en: The landing burn pays twice: cancel the orbital speed you are carrying, and hold yourself up against gravity the whole way down. Add them for the descent Δv.
cur: 着陆点火要付出双倍代价：既要抵消你所携带的轨道速度，又要在整个下降过程中对抗重力支撑自身。将两者相加即为下降 Δv。

en: You are circling the Moon. To land, first know how fast you are going — orbital speed here is far slower than at Earth, because the Moon pulls so much more gently.
cur: 你正环绕月球飞行。要着陆，首先要知道自己有多快——这里的轨道速度远低于地球，因为月球的引力要温和得多。

en: Landing is a controlled fall. To slow down and hover, your engine must out-push lunar gravity — thrust-to-weight above one, or you simply keep falling.
cur: 着陆是一次受控的坠落。要减速并悬停，你的引擎推力必须超过月球引力——推重比大于一，否则你只会一直坠落。

en: Does your lander carry enough Δv to cancel its orbit and settle softly onto the surface? Come up short and it is a crash, not a landing.
cur: 你的着陆器是否携带足够的 Δv 来抵消轨道速度并平稳落到地面？若不足，那便是坠毁，而非着陆。

en: Let go of a mass and gravity does the rest — it speeds up as it falls. How long does it take, and how fast is it at the bottom?
cur: 放开一个质量，剩下的交给引力——它在下落中加速。需要多久，落到底部时又有多快？

en: Throw a mass and gravity curves its path. The launch speed and angle set how far it flies before it lands.
cur: 抛出一个质量，引力使其轨迹弯曲。发射速度和角度决定它落地前飞多远。

en: The first principle of everything that flies: how a force changes a mass's motion. Master this one law and the rest of the Lab follows.
cur: 一切飞行之物的第一原理：力如何改变质量的运动。掌握这一条定律，实验室其余内容便水到渠成。

en: Leave low orbit and coast a quarter-million kilometres. Find the burn that stretches your path all the way out to the Moon.
cur: 离开低轨道，滑行二十五万公里。找到那次点火，将你的轨迹一路延伸至月球。

en: The cheapest way to raise your orbit is a stretched ellipse that just touches both: one burn to leave, a half-lap coast, one burn to arrive. Stretch it all the way out to the Moon.
cur: 抬升轨道最省的方法，是一条同时与两条轨道相切的拉长椭圆：一次点火离开，滑行半圈，再一次点火抵达。把它一直拉伸到月球。

en: Going straight up isn't enough — you'd just fall back. To stay up, go sideways fast enough that the ground curves away as fast as you fall. That speed is the circular orbital velocity.
cur: 直直向上飞是不够的——你只会掉回来。要留在天上，就得横向飞得足够快，让地面下沉的速度和你下坠的速度一样快。这个速度就是圆轨道速度。

en: Add the two burns: that is the Δv to reach the Moon FROM low Earth orbit — on top of the ~9.4 km/s it already took just to get to orbit. Does your on-orbit budget cover the transfer?
cur: 将两次点火相加：这就是从近地轨道抵达月球所需的Δv——此外还需约9.4 km/s才能进入轨道。你的在轨预算能否覆盖此次转移？

en: Orbits aren't all circles. Vis-viva gives your speed at any point of any orbit from just two numbers — where you are, and how big the orbit is. It's the tool every transfer is built from.
cur: 轨道并非都是圆形。活力公式仅凭两个数字——你所在的位置，以及轨道的大小——就能算出你在任意轨道任意点的速度。它是每一次转移的构建基石。

en: Orrery is a browser-based solar system explorer, mission simulator, and encyclopedia. Real orbital mechanics under the hood — Keplerian two-body propagation, Lambert solvers for transfer trajectories, the same equations real flight teams use. No backend. No accounts. en: The project started during the lead-up to Artemis II. NASA was about to send four humans around the Moon for the first time since 1972, and the public conversation around it was almost entirely uninformed. People didn't know what 'free-return trajectory' meant. They didn't know why Mars launch windows happen every 26 months. They didn't know the rocket equation.
cur: 这个项目始于Artemis II的筹备阶段。NASA即将送四名人类环绕月球，这是自1972年以来的首次，而围绕此事的公众讨论几乎完全缺乏了解。人们不知道"自由返回轨迹"是什么意思。他们不知道为什么火星发射窗口每26个月出现一次。他们不知道火箭方程。

en: Orrery is the answer to that. Spaceflight is built on physics that's been understood since Newton. Most of what looks magical is actually visible — you can see the orbits, you can compute the transfer arcs, you can read every formula. The simulator is the front door; the encyclopedia is the textbook; together they're the project.

en: Spaceflight is usually remembered as a string of missions and machines. But nothing here happened on its own — every rocket, every landing, every station was the work of a {program}: a sustained campaign, backed by a nation or a company, reaching for something specific. The programs are where the ambition lived and the rivalries played out. Read together, they are the whole arc of getting off the ground — from the first firsts of the Space Race to the stations, telescopes, and futures being built right now.
